findings.title: No Container Image Vulnerability Scan in CI
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:206-219,273-285,342-354 — Trivy image scan (scan-type: image, severity CRITICAL,HIGH, exit-code "1", ignore-unfixed) after each build on the push deploy path
.github/workflows/build-push.yml:49-62,121-133,202-214 — same image scan in the manual build pipeline (push triggers removed per build-push.yml:3-6)
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:1-60 and SECURITY.md:36-40 — document the image scan as part of the supply-chain controls
findings.impact: The deployed artifact (the OCI image) is gated on fixed HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs before deploy; the previous filesystem-only gap is closed for the three app images.
findings.recommendation: Keep the gate; extend scanning to the pinned third-party images (new finding) and add a scratch-branch test proving the gate fails on a known-vulnerable base.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: image scan present on the push deploy path (deploy-do.yml:206-219 etc., triggered on apps/infra/lockfile pushes per :16-29) and in the manual pipeline. Previous register marked verified-fixed at 9c0b88c; fix still effective.

findings.title: SBOM Is Lockfile-Only, Not an Image SBOM or Attestation
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:220-243,286-305,355-374 — trivy format: cyclonedx against the pushed digest (steps.build-*.outputs.digest) + actions/attest-sbom with push-to-registry: true
.github/workflows/build-push.yml:64-83,135-153,216-234 — image SBOM generation + 30-day artifact upload per image
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:1-60 — documents both artifacts (lockfile SBOM vs per-image SBOM) and the digest binding
findings.impact: An SBOM bound to the deployed image digest now exists and is attested as an OCI referrer, so incident response can answer "what shipped in this digest?".
findings.recommendation: Keep; retain the lockfile SBOM as a secondary artifact and re-verify the attestation on a real deployed digest.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: per-image CycloneDX SBOMs generated against the pushed digest on the deploy path and attested via actions/attest-sbom; docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md matches the implementation.

findings.title: Unsigned Images With No Provenance/Attestation
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:244-249,306-311,375-380 — actions/attest-build-provenance with push-to-registry: true per image
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:391-515 — verify-attestations job resolves each tag to a digest and runs gh attestation verify (fail closed; explicit reviewed allow-list for legacy rollback digests)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:537-562 — deploy job needs verify-attestations and requires its result == 'success'
.github/workflows/build-push.yml:85-90,155-160,236-241 — provenance attestation in the manual pipeline too
findings.impact: Images are cryptographically bound to this repository's workflow, and a missing/invalid attestation blocks the deploy — the substitution scenario is gated.
findings.recommendation: Keep; close the pull-by-tag TOCTOU (new finding) so the verified digest is the artifact that actually runs.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: provenance attestation produced and verified at deploy, fail-closed (residual: the droplet pulls by tag after digest verification — tracked as the new TOCTOU finding).

findings.title: Pinned Base-Image Digests Have No Automated Refresh
evidence: .github/dependabot.yml:41-92 — package-ecosystem: docker entries for /, /apps/api, /apps/web, /apps/worker, /infra/digitalocean (weekly, target-branch develop)
apps/api/Dockerfile:1,26; apps/web/Dockerfile:1,37; apps/worker/Dockerfile:1,25 — node:20-alpine@sha256:fb4cd12c… pinned in every stage
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:28,208,248,311 — redis/prometheus/alertmanager/caddy digest-pinned; docker-compose.yml:67 — Playwright e2e image digest-pinned
findings.impact: Base-image security patches now arrive as reviewed Dependabot PRs instead of unmanaged drift.
findings.recommendation: Keep; pair with the third-party image scan so a pinned digest is also checked for known CVEs between bumps.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 5 docker ecosystem entries cover all Dockerfiles/compose files (root entry covers the local Playwright pin). Previous register cited mainecybertech#146.

findings.title: Local Compose Ships Default Credentials and Repo-Wide Bind Mount
evidence: docker-compose.yml:63 — e2e service has profiles: ["e2e"], so a plain `docker compose up` never starts it
docker-compose.yml:80 — E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?set E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD (the local seed password is 1)} — no shipped default
docker-compose.yml:70-74 — repo-wide bind mount .:/app (rw) remains; the comment documents that the Playwright harness reads the working tree and writes report/auth artifacts
.github/workflows/e2e.yml:168 — CI e2e job still hardcodes E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD: 1 for its runner-local ephemeral stack
findings.impact: The weak-default credential path is closed for the compose stack; the residual repo-wide rw mount (local-only by design) still expands blast radius if the stack is ever run on a shared host.
findings.recommendation: Keep the profile + required-variable pattern; document the local-only constraint in README.dev.md; consider sourcing the CI seed password from a secret for parity.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: e2e is profile-gated and requires E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD explicitly (no default) — fix present (commit 7fc3f1f6). Residual: repo-wide rw bind mount (docker-compose.yml:72, documented) and the CI-only hardcode at .github/workflows/e2e.yml:168. Matches the previous register's partially-fixed assessment.

findings.title: Redis Password Exposed on Process Argument Vector
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:37 — user: redis; :42 — entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/usr/local/bin/redis-entrypoint.sh"]; :44 — REDIS_PASSWORD required with ${VAR:?}
infra/digitalocean/redis-entrypoint.sh:13-21 — umask 077; password written to /tmp/redis.conf (tmpfs); exec redis-server "$CONF" (never argv)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:56-61 — healthcheck authenticates via REDISCLI_AUTH env, not redis-cli -a
findings.impact: The password is no longer readable from `ps`/docker inspect args on the host; the redis container also runs as the unprivileged redis user.
findings.recommendation: Keep. Note the remaining env exposure (REDIS_PASSWORD in the container environment, visible to host root) is inherent to compose env injection and same-trust as /opt/mct-portal/.env (0600).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: password-file entrypoint and REDISCLI_AUTH healthcheck present; argv exposure closed (commit 84b843c2 / #32).

findings.title: Deploy Health Gate Ignores Worker Health
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:174-184 — worker healthcheck on http://127.0.0.1:3001/health with start_period: 30s
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:835-847 — compose-level gate requires api AND web AND worker healthy (18 attempts, 10s apart)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:905-922 — post-deploy worker probe over SSH; failure prints logs, exits 1 and triggers rollback
findings.impact: A worker that never becomes healthy now fails the deploy and reverts instead of shipping silently.
findings.recommendation: Keep; include the observability services in a post-deploy probe (new finding).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: worker health is fatal in both the compose health gate and the SSH probe.

findings.title: No Container Resource/PID Limits Beyond Memory
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:55,118,166,200,236,300,337 — pids_limit on all 7 services (redis 128, api/worker/web/prometheus 256, alertmanager/caddy 128)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:51,114,162,199,232,299,336 — mem_limit on all 7 services
docker-compose.yml — local dev compose has no pids_limit/mem_limit on api/web/worker (dev-only residual)
findings.impact: A single container can no longer exhaust the host PID table and take down the single-droplet topology.
findings.recommendation: Keep; consider adding pids_limit to the local dev compose for parity (optional).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: pids_limit count is 7/7 prod services (commit c5b579be / #51). Residual: local dev compose lacks limits (dev-only).

findings.title: Missing `--start-period` on API and Worker Healthchecks
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:127-128 — api healthcheck start_period: 30s
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:182-184 — worker healthcheck start_period: 30s
docker-compose.yml:17,56 — local api/worker healthchecks also set start_period: 30s
apps/api/Dockerfile:58 and apps/worker/Dockerfile:57 — image-level HEALTHCHECK still lacks --start-period (residual, tracked as a new finding)
findings.impact: Boot-time failures no longer count against the compose healthcheck retry budget on the deployed paths.
findings.recommendation: Keep; add --start-period to the image-level healthchecks for parity with apps/web/Dockerfile:73.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: both compose paths set start_period: 30s (commit c2bdb59a / #125). Residual: Dockerfile-level api/worker healthchecks still lack it — see new finding.

findings.title: Broad `.dockerignore` `*.md`/`*.txt`/`*.log` Could Mask Needed Build Files
evidence: .dockerignore:50-52 — *.md, *.txt, *.log patterns still present
find apps/api apps/web apps/worker packages -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.log' (excluding node_modules) — no matches; apps/web/public contains no .txt (favicon/manifest/sw only)
no build script or config reads a .md/.txt/.log file (grep over apps/*/src, next.config, packages)
findings.impact: No active breakage today, but a future build-relevant file (e.g. robots.txt added to apps/web/public) would be silently dropped from the image.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the patterns to known-unneeded paths (docs/, **/README.md, CHANGELOG.md) or add explicit ! re-includes for build-relevant files; add a build-time assertion for expected public assets.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: patterns unchanged since 20261002-0344; no currently-masked required file found (find returned nothing). Previous register carried it as open/not-re-verified.

findings.title: Deploy verifies attestations by digest but pulls and runs images by tag (TOCTOU)
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:501-514 — verify-attestations resolves ${GHCR_PREFIX}/${img}:${IMAGE_TAG} to a digest and runs gh attestation verify on that digest
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:786-788 — the deploy job then docker pull's ${prefix}/mct-:${IMAGE_TAG} (tag), minutes later and on a different runner
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:69,131,187 — services reference images by ${IMAGE_TAG} tag, not digest
findings.impact: An actor with GHCR write access (or a compromised token) can move the tag to a different, unattested digest between verification and pull; the droplet then runs it — the exact substitution the gate exists to stop.
findings.recommendation: Emit each verified digest from verify-attestations ($GITHUB_OUTPUT) and pass it to the deploy job; pull/run image@sha256:… (compose image refs can interpolate per-image digest variables), or re-verify on the droplet immediately before `up`.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: static analysis of the verify→pull sequence; exploitability depends on GHCR tag mutability/package settings, which are not verifiable from the repo.

findings.title: Caddy runs with a writable rootfs and a writable Caddyfile bind mount
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:310-337 — caddy has cap_drop: ALL + cap_add: [NET_BIND_SERVICE] but no read_only and no tmpfs (api/web/prometheus/alertmanager all set read_only: true)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:320 — ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile (no :ro), while certs at :321 are mounted :ro
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:322-323 — caddy-data:/data and caddy-config:/config volumes already carry writable state
findings.impact: A process inside the caddy container can modify the host's /opt/mct-portal/Caddyfile (persisting across restarts) and write anywhere in its rootfs; a caddy compromise can tamper with TLS termination/content for all users.
findings.recommendation: Mount the Caddyfile :ro, set read_only: true with tmpfs: [/tmp] (state is in the volumes), and consider user: caddy if the image can bind 80/443 with the granted capability.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; docker compose config assertion test suggested.

findings.title: Prometheus has no healthcheck and observability is outside the deploy health gate
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:207-237 — prometheus service defines no healthcheck (redis, caddy and alertmanager all do)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:835-847 — deploy health gate checks only api, web and worker
commits 00cb3da6 / f025e95c — recent METRICS_TOKEN/scrape-path fixes show the monitoring path can silently break while deploys stay green
findings.impact: A prometheus container that fails to start or load config, or that cannot authenticate the API scrape, is not detected by the deploy or rollback logic; docker compose ps still reports it running.
findings.recommendation: Add healthcheck: wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy (30s interval, 20s start-period) and extend the compose gate or add a post-deploy probe covering prometheus/alertmanager/redis/caddy.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; overlaps the observability domain but is a container health-gate gap.

findings.title: Image-level HEALTHCHECK for api and worker lacks `--start-period`
evidence: apps/api/Dockerfile:58 — HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 (no --start-period)
apps/worker/Dockerfile:57 — same; apps/web/Dockerfile:73 — has --start-period=40s
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:122-128,174-184 and docker-compose.yml:12-17,51-56 — compose paths override with start_period: 30s
findings.impact: Any docker run / non-compose orchestrator uses the image default and can mark a slow-booting container unhealthy and restart it; only compose paths are covered.
findings.recommendation: Add --start-period=20s to both image healthchecks for parity with web and compose.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; residual of the compose-level CTR-P3-001 fix.

findings.title: infra/digitalocean operator docs and `.env.example` drift from the deployed stack
evidence: infra/digitalocean/README.md:9-16 — service table lists api/web/worker/redis/caddy/prometheus but omits alertmanager (infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:244-307)
infra/digitalocean/README.md:45-51 — supporting files omit redis-entrypoint.sh, alertmanager.tmpl.yml and metrics-token

infra/digitalocean/.env.example — omits METRICS_TOKEN, ALERTMANAGER_*, M365_CLIENT_STATE, JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET, JSM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED (all referenced by infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:88-92,252-266)
docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md:233 — 'web ... current: 256MB' vs infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:199 mem_limit: 512m
findings.impact: Operators following the README/.env.example under-provision the dead-man's switch and metrics auth, and the OOM runbook points at the wrong limit.
findings.recommendation: Update the README service table + supporting files, sync .env.example with the compose env keys, and correct the handbook mem_limit (secret-matrix portion cross-refs SECRET-P2-001).
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; doc drift verified by grep (no alertmanager/redis-entrypoint/metrics-token matches in README.md) and line comparison for mem_limit.

findings.title: Third-party pinned images are not vulnerability-scanned in CI
evidence: grep -n image-ref: deploy-do.yml build-push.yml — Trivy image scans target only mct-api/mct-worker/mct-web
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:28,208,248,311 — redis:7-alpine, prom/prometheus:v3.5.1, prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1, caddy:2-alpine pinned by digest but never scanned by any workflow
.github/dependabot.yml:84-92 — Dependabot only refreshes the pins weekly (a vulnerable digest can remain deployed until the PR lands)
findings.impact: A pinned third-party digest that later becomes known-vulnerable (notably the internet-facing caddy) is not gated; discovery depends on external advisories and manual action.
findings.recommendation: Add a scheduled + workflow_dispatch job that pulls the four pinned refs and runs Trivy (CRITICAL,HIGH, exit-code 1), reporting through the existing alerting path; keep Dependabot for bumps.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; image scans exist but only for the built app images.

findings.title: No Dockerfile lint gate in CI
evidence: grep -rn hadolint .github/ package.json scripts/ tools/ — no matches (no lint step, no .hadolint.yaml)
apps/web/Dockerfile:59-62 — manual hadolint DL3045 fix (explicit WORKDIR) present but unguarded
build-push.yml/deploy-do.yml — no docker buildx build --check step
findings.impact: Dockerfile hygiene fixes (WORKDIR, shell-form healthchecks) can silently regress with no CI signal.
findings.recommendation: Add a SHA-pinned hadolint (or docker buildx build --check) step to the PR/validate gate and document the expected rules.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; complements SUPPLY-P3-002 (manual lint fixes, no gate).

report:
# Container Runtime Security Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive (full hardening edition)
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (read-only worktree `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d` (`8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd`, 2026-10-11)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent 36 (area code CTR)
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/36_container_runtime_security.md`
- Scope limitations:
  - Static review only. `docker` is not installed in the audit environment, so no image was built, run, pulled, or scanned; pinned digests were not resolved against a registry; image size and runtime behaviour are `not reproducible`.
  - No droplet or lab access was authorized/used, so "running container configuration vs declared configuration" is `Unknown` (checked repo-side only).
  - No secret values are printed; secret-like config is referenced by `path:line` + type.

## Scope

Reviewed at `8d299b8d`:

- Dockerfiles: `apps/api/Dockerfile`, `apps/web/Dockerfile`, `apps/worker/Dockerfile`
- Compose: `docker-compose.yml` (local/dev), `infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml` (prod)
- Build context: `.dockerignore`
- Entrypoints/health: `infra/digitalocean/redis-entrypoint.sh`, `apps/api/src/main.ts`, `apps/worker/src/{consumer-bullmq,consumer-sqs,logger}.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/logger.ts`
- CI/CD: `.github/workflows/{deploy-do,build-push,e2e,sbom,test}.yml`, `.github/actions/dependency-audit/action.yml`, `.github/dependabot.yml`
- Operator docs: `infra/digitalocean/{README.md,.env.example,Caddyfile*}`, `docs/{SBOM_PROCESS,CI,FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK,ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES}.md`, `SECURITY.md`
- Previous run: `runs/mainecybertech-20261004-full-main-9c0b88c/{follow_up_register,risk_register}.md` (all 10 CTR rows)

Not reviewed: image layers/registry manifests, GitHub environment settings, droplet runtime state, Terraform/cloud-init (domain 12), secret rotation inventory (domain 38).

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/api/Dockerfile`, `apps/worker/Dockerfile` | Dockerfile | API/worker build + runtime | 2 stages, digest-pinned `node:20-alpine`, `USER appuser`, `--prod --ignore-scripts`, HEALTHCHECK, npm/corepack removed |
| `apps/web/Dockerfile` | Dockerfile | Web build + runtime | 3 stages, digest-pinned base, `USER nextjs`, standalone bundle, `--chown`, HEALTHCHECK with start-period |
| `docker-compose.yml` | Compose (local) | Dev/e2e stack | e2e profile-gated + password required; repo-wide rw bind mount remains; no caps/limits |
| `infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml` | Compose (prod) | Deployed stack (7 services) | `x-security` (cap_drop ALL + no-new-privileges), read_only×5, pids_limit×7, mem_limit, log caps, digest pins |
| `.dockerignore` | Build hygiene | Context reduction / secret exclusion | `.env*` excluded; broad `*.md/*.txt/*.log` still present |
| `infra/digitalocean/redis-entrypoint.sh` | Entrypoint | Redis secret handling | 0600 `/tmp/redis.conf`, password off argv |
| `.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml` | CI/CD (push path) | Build → scan → SBOM → attest → verify → deploy | 3 image scans, attest-sbom, attest-build-provenance, `gh attestation verify` gate, health gate incl. worker |
| `.github/workflows/build-push.yml` | CI/CD (manual) | Reusable build pipeline | same scan/SBOM/attest steps; push triggers removed |
| `.github/dependabot.yml` | Automation | Digest refresh | 5 `docker` entries (root, apps/*, infra/digitalocean) |
| `docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md`, `SECURITY.md` | Docs | Claims about scanning/SBOM/attestation | Image SBOM + attestation documented; third-party images not covered |
| `infra/digitalocean/README.md`, `.env.example`, `docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md` | Docs | Declared operator config | Drift found (see finding) |

## Verification Performed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grep -c "pids_limit" infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml` | static check | CTR-P2-005 | `7` — every prod service has a PID cap (128–256) |
| `grep -n "read_only" infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml` | static check | Read-only FS | 5×`true` (api/worker/web/prometheus/alertmanager), 1×`false` (redis, documented), caddy absent |
| `grep -rn "docker.sock\|privileged: true\|/var/run/docker"` (repo, non-node_modules) | static check | Socket/mount privilege | no matches — no docker socket or privileged container anywhere |
| `grep -rn "trivy\|attest\|sbom" .github/` | static check | CTR-P1-001/002/003 | image scans, image SBOMs, `attest-sbom`/`attest-build-provenance`, `gh attestation verify` all present |
| `grep -n "image-ref:" deploy-do.yml build-push.yml` | static check | Scan coverage | only `mct-api`/`mct-worker`/`mct-web` — third-party images unscanned |
| `grep -n "start_period" apps/*/Dockerfile infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml docker-compose.yml` | static check | CTR-P3-001 | compose paths set 30s (api/worker); Dockerfile api/worker still lack it; web Dockerfile has 40s |
| `grep -n "E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD\|profiles" docker-compose.yml .github/workflows/e2e.yml` | static check | CTR-P2-002 | compose requires `${E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?}` and profile-gates e2e; CI workflow still hardcodes `1` for the ephemeral runner-local stack |
| `find apps/api apps/web apps/worker packages -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.log'` | static check | CTR-P3-002 | no matches — broad ignore patterns currently mask nothing needed by builds |
| `grep -rn "hadolint" .github/ package.json scripts/ tools/` | static check | Lint gate | no matches — no Dockerfile lint in CI |
| `grep -n -i "alertmanager\|redis-entrypoint\|metrics-token" infra/digitalocean/README.md` | static check | Docs drift | no matches — README omits services/files that exist in compose |
| `grep -rn ":latest" --include=*.yml --include=Dockerfile* .` | static check | Latest tags | no matches (only the `.env.example` placeholder `IMAGE_TAG=latest`) |
| `git status --porcelain` | safety | Read-only audit | clean — no target changes |

**Exact commands and observed results**

- `cd /tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target && git log -1 --format='%H %s'` → `8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd Merge PR #168: promote develop to main`.
- `find . -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*compose*'` → exactly 3 Dockerfiles and 2 compose files (inventory is closed; no stray container files in `templates/`).
- `grep -c pids_limit infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml` → `7` (redis 128, api 256, worker 256, web 256, prometheus 256, alertmanager 128, caddy 128).
- `grep -n "read_only" infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml` → lines 31 (`false`, redis), 121, 169, 201, 237, 301 (`true`); caddy has none.
- `grep -rn "docker.sock|privileged: true"` → no matches.
- `find apps/api apps/web apps/worker packages -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.log'` (non-node_modules) → empty.
- `grep -n "E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD" .github/workflows/e2e.yml` → line 168 `E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD: 1` (ephemeral CI stack only).
- `grep -n "mem_limit" docs/FINAL_DEPLOYMENT_OPERATIONS_HANDBOOK.md` → line 233 says web is 256MB; `infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:199` says `512m` (drift).
- `grep -n "provenance-verification-at-deploy" docs/CI.md` → line 49, the SECURITY.md link anchor exists.
- Runtime verification (`docker build`/`docker inspect`/`trivy image`/`gh attestation verify`) → `not reproducible` (no docker/registry/droplet access).

**Claim verdicts (headline claims in this area)**

| Claim | Source | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "every image is scanned with Trivy after build and before deploy" | `SECURITY.md:36-40` | `supported` for the 3 app images; `not applicable` to the 4 third-party images (new finding) |
| "the deploy pipeline verifies that attestation before pulling" | `SECURITY.md:37-44`, `deploy-do.yml:391-515` | `partially supported` — verification is by digest, the droplet then pulls by tag (TOCTOU; new finding) |
| "prod containers drop all capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only" | `infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:3-7,121,169,201` | `supported` for api/worker/web/prometheus/alertmanager; redis is `read_only:false` (documented) and caddy is writable (new finding) |
| "worker health is fatal to the deploy" | `deploy-do.yml:905-922` | `supported` |
| "redis password is off argv" | `redis-entrypoint.sh:13-21`, compose:42,58 | `supported`; the value remains in the container environment (`docker inspect` for host root) |
| "digest pins are refreshed automatically" | `dependabot.yml:41-92` | `supported` (weekly docker PRs for all four locations) |

## Executive Summary

The container posture remains strong and the previous run's CTR findings are almost entirely fixed at `8d299b8d`: the deploy path (not just the manual build pipeline) scans each app image with Trivy before `up`, generates digest-bound CycloneDX image SBOMs, attests both SBOM and build provenance, and gates the deploy on `gh attestation verify`; Dependabot refreshes all digest pins; redis keeps its password off argv; every prod service has a PID cap; api/worker healthchecks have `start_period` in both compose files; and the worker is now a fatal part of the deploy health gate.

The remaining gaps are narrower: a tag→digest TOCTOU between attestation verification and the droplet pull (P2), the third-party pinned images (redis/caddy/prometheus/alertmanager) never being vulnerability-scanned, caddy running with a writable rootfs and a writable Caddyfile bind mount, prometheus lacking a healthcheck while observability sits outside the deploy gate, image-level api/worker healthchecks still missing `--start-period`, operator docs drifting from the deployed stack (alertmanager omitted from the README; handbook mem_limit stale), and no Dockerfile lint gate. The local dev compose remains intentionally unhardened; its only residual from the previous register is the documented repo-wide rw bind mount (plus a hardcoded ephemeral test password in the CI e2e workflow).

Recommended next actions: (1) make the deploy pull by the verified digest, (2) add a scheduled scan of the four pinned third-party images, (3) `:ro` the Caddyfile and `read_only: true` caddy, (4) add a prometheus healthcheck and include observability in the gate, (5) add hadolint + `--start-period` parity, (6) refresh the infra README/.env.example/handbook.

**Overall Domain Score: 4.1 / 5** (production-ready, hardened runtime; gaps are the TOCTOU window, unscanned third-party images, and a few per-service hardening/documentation items).

### Finding: Deploy verifies attestations by digest but pulls and runs images by tag (TOCTOU) (new)

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: Medium · Area: CTR · Status: open

- What is happening: verification and execution resolve the tag independently; an actor with GHCR write access (or a compromised token) could move the tag to a different, unattested digest between the two jobs, and the droplet would run it.

- Suggested validation: in a scratch environment, push an image, verify, retag to a second digest, and assert the deploy uses the verified digest only.
- Owner: platform/infrastructure · Effort: S–M · Dependencies: attestation gate (present)
- Status: open — new finding at 8d299b8d.

### Finding: Third-party pinned images are not vulnerability-scanned in CI (new)

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: High · Area: CTR · Status: open
- Evidence: `grep -n "image-ref:" deploy-do.yml build-push.yml` → only `mct-api`/`mct-worker`/`mct-web`; no workflow scans `redis:7-alpine` (`infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:28`), `caddy:2-alpine` (`:311`), `prom/prometheus` (`:208`), `prom/alertmanager` (`:248`); `.github/dependabot.yml:84-92` only refreshes the pins weekly.
- What is happening: a digest that later becomes known-vulnerable can stay in production until a Dependabot PR lands and is merged; nothing gates it.
- Recommended fix: add a scheduled + dispatchable job that pulls the four pinned refs and runs Trivy (`severity: CRITICAL,HIGH`, `exit-code: 1`), reporting via the existing alerting path; keep Dependabot for the bump.
- Suggested validation: run the job against the current digests; seed a known-vuln digest in a scratch branch and assert failure.
- Owner: platform/infrastructure · Effort: S · Dependencies: registry access (public images)
- Status: open — new finding at 8d299b8d.

### Finding: No Dockerfile lint gate in CI (new)

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: High · Area: CTR · Status: open

- Recommended fix: add hadolint (SHA-pinned action or container) to the PR/validate gate, plus optional `docker buildx build --check`; keep the existing digest-pin practice.
- Owner: platform/CI owner · Effort: S · Dependencies: none
